ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher within the NS-7 process; no driver account action.

rejected_claims.reason: The pre-acceptance-to-cancellation clock (5 min 50 s, [F4]) only shows NS-4's rider-side window was open; NS-4 does not govern a driver cancellation, which NS-0 routes through NS-1/NS-2 [F4][NS-0][NS-4]. It proves nothing about the wait at the pickup [F4][NS-1].
Approaching the 3-minute mark is failing it: NS-1 (iii) needs > 180 s and the records show 150 s inside 200 m [F2] and 120 s stationary [F3], with only 100 s after the tap [F6][NS-1].

Chat notices [F10][F11] do not create the chargeable wait; NS-1 (iii) is a numeric GPS/timeline condition that stands at 2 min 30 s [F2][F6], and the 14:14 assertion of a >3-minute wait is a self-serving statement that loses to the system records [F11][F2][F5][NS-1].
NS-2 applies precisely because NS-1 (iii) fails; the arrival limb being satisfied is not enough, and the $6.61 charged [F8] must therefore be refunded [F2][F6][F8][NS-2].

Profile facts never decide a case, and both parties show 0 upheld disputes, so [F16][F17] supply no basis to prefer the driver's account and none of the missing seconds of wait [F16][F17][F2][F3][NS-1].
Accepted in part: (i) and (ii) are satisfied [F6][F1], but this only frames the issue; the refund rests on the failure of NS-1 (iii) [F2][F3][NS-1], not on the location of the tap [F6][F1][NS-1].
The rider's clean profile [F16] is not the basis for the refund; profile facts cannot decide the case, and the outcome follows from the failed wait-duration limb [F16][F2][F3][NS-7].

The no traffic/weather facts [F13][F14][F15] are immaterial to NS-3, which addresses driver cancellations without a claimed no-show; here the driver claimed a no-show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern [F11][F12][F13][F14][NS-3][NS-1][NS-2].
